Real caller found independently: _Func_impl<lambda_263f3dc4>::vf2 at 0x116ea4 does r0=[r1] (platform), r1=[this+4] (callback), ldr.w r3,[vtable,#0x8c], blx -> plain AAPCS r0=this, r1=callback, no stack args. That lambda lives next to sub_1180fc which is the only user of the 'custom.png' string, i.e. it is the skin-picker flow. Bytes at 0x5830F8 = 2d e9 80 48 0d f1 04 0b 8d b0 6f 46 6f f0 01 03, function length 0x50. Only data xref is the vtable cell. Nit: the cited lambda vf2 is actually 0x58e5c0 (-> b.w 0x5875ac); 0x58e5d0 is its vf0/copy. Chain conclusion is unchanged.

0x13695A4 + 0x8c = 0x1369630; ptrs shows 0x009830F9 = ImageBase 0x400000 + 0x5830F8 + 1. Cell lies in .data (0x132F000..0x15BD580), writable. Base reloc type 3 applies to the cell at load, so runtime value is real_base+0x5830F9; comparing against that before patching is correct.

bytes 5830f8 -> 2d e9 80 48 0d f1 04 0b 8d b0 6f 46 (push.w {r7,fp,lr}; add.w fp,sp,#4; sub sp,#0x34; mov r7,sp). The ldr.w pc,[pc] 8-byte alternative is fine (function is 0x50 bytes) but unnecessary.

0x3b4 verified independently in 5 functions: pickFile 0x583114 ldr.w r0,[r0,#0x3b4]; vf36 0x583a46; ctor 0x5816ae (add.w r6,r4,#0x3b4) + store at 0x581810; sub_582174 0x582220; plus many AppPlatform_Winrt vfs (vf45/47/96, requestRelativeMouse...) at 0x5827d6..0x582bb4 using ldr.w r0,[r0,#0x3b4]. pickFile passes the loaded adapter into the lambda capture (strd r3,r0,[r7]) and the cancel lambda reads [[this+4]+0xa8], confirming the adapter semantics.

pickFile 0x583120 str.w r1,[r0,#0xa8] with r0=adapter; cancel lambda 0x58e608: ldr r3,[r0,#4] (captured adapter); ldr.w r3,[r3,#0xa8]; mov r0,r3; ldr r3,[r3]; ldr r3,[r3,#8]; blx r3. Success lambda 0x58776c reads [r0,#0xa8] the same way.

Cancel lambda 0x58e608 and success lambda 0x587780..0x58783c (r6==0 branch: mov r0,r3; ldr r3,[r3]; ... [r3,#8]; blx) call vtable+8 with r0=callback only. Callback is a std::function-style _Func_impl, whose slot 2 is _Do_call (consistent with MSVC _Func_base layout vf0/vf1 copy/move, vf2 do_call, vf3 target_type seen in the dumped vtables). Void return, no extra args. Note the success path with a real file (r6!=0) goes through async sub_58a628 first; the host does not need to emulate that.

ABI re-derived from the callee (r0->r6 this, r1->r8 path read via [r8+0x14]/[r8]/[r8+0x10], r2->r5 out string cleared in place with len=0 and cap/data via [r5+0x14]/[r5], r3 tested -> vtable[8] (+0x20) check) and from two independent callers: lang loader sub_5eab30 (0x5eabb0..0x5eabc0: r0=obj, r1=path, r2=&out, r3=0, blx [vtable+0x2c]) and the generic ResourcePackStack::vf1 0x64c608 (0x64c6e2..0x64c708: r1=r8 path, r2=out, r3=0, blx [vt+0x2c]) which is the multi-pack lookup path and is the likely route for ui/*.json. RTTI ZipPackAccessStrategy vtable 0x136E56C, +0x2c = 0x136E598 holds 0x00A4E6B9. Vtable stride 0x50 = 19 slots, with the next vtable's COL pointer at +0x4c, so slot 11 is unambiguous.

RTTI ZipPackAccessStrategyOwningFileAcccess vtable 0x136E5BC, +0x2c = 0x136E5E8 holds 0x00A4E6B9 (same pointer as the plain one). Extra finding: in the production factory (sub_633c94 -> zip factory sub_634344 -> sub_6347ac/sub_63484c -> sub_64ec30) the object created is the OWNING-file-access variant; the plain ZipPackAccessStrategy ctor sub_64d9e8 is only reached from sub_64ec30 (base ctor) and from unit-test code (sub_936b0/sub_939b4, 'stuff/more_stuff.json'). So the owning cell is the zip cell that matters.

RTTI DirectoryPackAccessStrategy vtable 0x136DF00, +0x2c = 0x136DF2C holds 0x00A314BD -> function 0x6314BC, pdata start, bytes 2d e9 f0 48 0d f1 10 0b ad f5 8a 6d 6f 46 14 46 (expected_bytes ok). Prologue: r0 this, r1 path (r6), r2 out (r4), r3 flag -> vtable[8]; the 24-byte string move into [r4] at 0x631556..0x631588; returns (out.size!=0). Data check: Minecraft_1.2.8.0_ARM32 contains no *.zip, vanilla/texts/en_US.lang and vanilla/ui/start_screen.json are plain loose files. Factory correction (does not change the hook): sub_634344 is the ZIP factory (it only picks MemoryMappedFileAccess vs FileSystemFileAccess and builds the owning zip strategy via sub_64ec30); the directory-vs-zip selector is sub_633c94 (calls sub_634344 for zip, sub_6342cc for Directory, sub_63430c for DirectoryWithEncryption, chosen by sub_633af0). Finder's 'factory sub_634344 chooses between directory and zip' is wrong, but the conclusion (hook all three) stands. Keep confidence medium: which strategy the vanilla pack actually gets is only static.

Cell 0x136E004 = 0xA323F1 (fn 0x6323F0, DirectoryPackWithEncryptionAccessStrategy vtable 0x136DFD8 + 0x2c) verified. The 'which original pointer to call' problem for the shared wrapper: zip cells (0x136E598, 0x136E5E8) share original 0x64E6B8|1 but the directory cell needs 0x6314BC|1 (and optionally encrypted 0x6323F0|1). The finder mentions this in notes but the x86 patch_128_zip_slot structure (one global 'original') would silently break on ARM; port_instructions should say to keep three separate originals/wrappers.
